clue.text: Lover go-go dancing around Italy and Luxembourg

indicators.note: dancing around says the letters of go-go jig about, with the two country letters mixed among them

parts.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy
L is the international vehicle code for Luxembourg

explanation.surface: A dancer in a go-go club whirls around on a European tour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing around' shuffles GOGO together with I and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A kept man paid by an older woman is her paid companion, a lover by trade.

clue.text: Very contorted tree getting support that's essential to staying upright

indicators.note: contorted means the word tree is twisted into a new order

parts.note: a bra is an item of supporting underwear

explanation.surface: A twisted tree is propped up so it can keep standing.
explanation.definitionFit: Each bone of the spinal column helps hold the body erect, so one is essential to standing straight.

clue.text: Broadcast excusing arresting Italian, one that should improve the atmosphere

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it

indicators.note: arresting means holding the other pieces captive inside

parts.note: condoning wrongdoing is excusing it
IT is Italian vermouth, as in gin and it
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A news report excuses the police for detaining an Italian suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooling and cleaning systems in buildings make the indoor air more pleasant to breathe.

definitions.meaning: serious and important, as a serious matter

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both physically heavy and serious or momentous.

clue.text: One looking into past pressure over allegations 'too corrupt'

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the first piece sits above the rest

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for pressure in physics

indicators.note: corrupt means the letters of the words allegations and too are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: A scandal: pressure over claims of corruption deemed too serious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' shuffles ALLEGATIONS TOO into ALAEONTOLOGIST, placed under P.
explanation.definitionFit: A fossil scientist studies ancient life, literally looking into the distant past.

indicators.note: can be signals that the letters of an alto may be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: An alto singer can sometimes sing out of tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' says AN ALTO's six letters can be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Music without a key centre sounds harsh and unharmonious to traditional ears.

clue.text: Birds, the ones with possessions in the East End

indicators.note: Cockneys of London's East End famously drop their aitches, so the opening H goes

parts.note: the haves are the wealthy, as in the haves and the have-nots

explanation.surface: Wealthy people's possessions in London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is the traditional Cockney district of London, where H is dropped from speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Aves is the scientific Latin name for the class containing all feathered creatures.

clue.text: Return of Bette Midler netting very little money

indicators.note: Return of says the hidden letters are read backwards
netting means catching in a net, so the words Bette Midler hold the letters inside them

explanation.surface: A Bette Midler comeback that earns almost nothing at the box office.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'netting' in the definition, but it is the indicator that the letters lie within Bette Midler; 'Return of' then reverses them. The definition is just 'very little money'.
explanation.definitionFit: A US ten-cent coin is a tiny sum of money.

indicators.note: not means the letter for feminine must be taken away

parts.note: fire is passion, ardour

explanation.surface: An angry outburst that is passionate but unladylike.
explanation.definitionFit: Ire is a literary synonym for anger or fury.

clue.text: Spirited revival of musical capturing dramatic ending

indicators.note: capturing means the rearranged show holds the other letter inside
a revival brings back the show in a new form, so its title's letters are rearranged

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical

indicators.note: ending picks the last letter of dramatic

explanation.surface: A lively revival of a stage musical with a dramatic finale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revival of' rearranges EVITA to ATIVE; 'capturing' puts C (from 'ending' of dramatic) inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Lively and energetic, an active person is full of spirit.

definitions.meaning: creative, expressive in a literary way
the phrase ... justice means fitting retribution

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means creative or expressive, and it also forms the phrase for fitting retribution.

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a looking glass is a mirror

indicators.note: reflected suits a mirror: the word for rear is read backwards

parts.note: the end is the rear part

explanation.surface: Joy turns to admire her bottom in the mirror.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joy' looks like a woman's name in the surface but is the definition; 'reflected' suits the mirror and signals the reversal, and 'in' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Happiness and delight are synonyms for this state of being glad.

parts.note: a motorbike with sidecar is called a combination, so a lock for it is jokingly named after it

explanation.definitionFit: A dial padlock opened by a number sequence shares its name with a bike-and-sidecar outfit.

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
on means working, as a machine that is switched on

explanation.surface: A fraudster nabbed while running a scam.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindle or scam is a fiddle in British slang.

clue.text: Bound to wear suit for cinema

indicators.note: to wear puts the jump inside, like a body inside clothes

parts.note: to fit is to suit
to bound is to leap

explanation.surface: Someone forced to wear a suit to go to the pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: A fleapit is British slang for a shabby old cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang term names a run-down picture house, supposedly infested with insects.

definitions.meaning: an American parks a car in a parking ...
a ... of things is a heap of them

explanation.definitionFit: The word is American for a car park and also means a large quantity.

clue.text: Trainee model nude in Times, following Sun

indicators.note: following places the remaining letters after the first one

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for Sunday

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: T stands for time, so two of them give times

indicators.note: model means the letters of nude are shaped into a new form

explanation.surface: A nude model photographed for one newspaper after appearing in another.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times and the Sun are both British newspapers, which is the surface's misdirection; 'model' is the anagram signal, 'in' the container and 'following' the order.
explanation.definitionFit: A learner in training at a college or university studies under supervision.

indicators.note: acoustically says the phrase is judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a record is a disc; lame means flawed or weak, as a lame excuse

explanation.surface: Someone denies that their record has faults in its sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acoustically' means DISC LAME is said out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: To renounce or reject responsibility for something is to deny it.

parts.note: an Aga is a range cooker that heats a farmhouse kitchen, and a saga is a long story

explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is a British range cooker; the term names a genre of novel set in comfortable middle-class rural homes.
explanation.definitionFit: The genre label joins a heating stove with a long story, so a story by the stove.

parts.note: sticking means holding fast
to plaster is to coat a wall

explanation.surface: Putting on a coat and holding it closed.
explanation.walkthrough: Sticking plaster is British for an adhesive bandage.
explanation.definitionFit: An adhesive bandage for a small cut is a wound dressing.

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped opening sounds of words, so the two pieces trade their starts

parts.note: a hoe is a garden implement
caught means seized

explanation.surface: A musical group's equipment has been confiscated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spooner exclaims' swaps the openings of HOE CAUGHT by sound, giving CO-HAWT.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of people with something in common, like a Roman army unit, is a band.

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang the word is also a verb meaning to listen in.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is a pincered garden creepy-crawly, and also a verb for listening in secretly.

indicators.note: restraining means holding the other piece inside

parts.note: giving thanks is giving credit
the OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: An actor's screen credit hemmed in by a court order.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hollywood star of Forrest Gump and Big is a famous film performer.

indicators.note: cut says a slice is taken from inside the words hip-hop album

explanation.surface: A Rolling Stone's hip-hop record has been trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' signals the letters within hip-hop album.
explanation.definitionFit: An iridescent gemstone is a precious stone.

clue.text: To spare first learner abandoning crashed Allegro …

indicators.note: crashed means the car name is smashed into a new arrangement
abandoning means one letter is left out of the car name
first picks the opening letter of learner

explanation.surface: A learner driver walks away from a crashed Austin Allegro.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' drops L (from 'first' of learner) from ALLEGRO; 'crashed' rearranges ALEGRO. The Allegro was a British Leyland car.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in plenty, more than enough, is available in abundance.

clue.text: … Acura trundled, taking in road avoiding traffic

indicators.note: taking in says the answer is held within the words Acura trundled

explanation.surface: An Acura car rolls slowly along a quiet back road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking in' signals letters inside Acura trundled. A rat run is British for a back street used as a short cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor residential street used by drivers to bypass congestion is a short cut away from jams.

clue.text: What might come in main talk

definitions.meaning: fuel supplied through a ... main pipe

explanation.definitionFit: Fuel delivered by underground pipe, and also informal chatter.

clue.text: One's tender in the same place

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, and 's is possessive
a bid is a tender, an offer

explanation.surface: Someone's offer made at the same location.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin abbreviation used in references means from the same source or place.
